en: Who is that? - That's Ann.
current: Хто то? - То Анн.
issue: The name Ann should be declined in Ukrainian.
fix: Хто то? - То Анна.

en: Whose toy is that? - That's its toy.
current: Чия то іграшка? - Це її іграшка.
issue: The possessive pronoun for 'its' should be 'його', not 'її'.
fix: Чия то іграшка? - Це його іграшка.

en: thirty one shoes - thirty two shoes
current: тридцять одне взуття - тридцять два взуття
issue: The word 'взуття' is a collective noun and doesn't usually take plural numbers like 'тридцять одне взуття' unless referring to types of footwear. 'Тридцять одне взуття' sounds unnatural when trying to express 'thirty one shoes'. It would be more natural to say 'thirty one pairs of shoes' or specify the type of shoe.
fix: тридцять один черевик - тридцять два черевики

en: one lady - five ladies
current: одна пані - п'ять панянок
issue: The plural form 'панянок' is not the correct plural of 'пані'.
fix: одна пані - п'ять пані

en: There isn't little milk in the carton.
current: У пакеті немало молока.
issue: The English phrase 'There isn't little milk' means 'There is a lot of milk' or 'There is much milk'. The Ukrainian translation 'немало молока' means 'quite a lot of milk' or 'not little milk'. The English phrase 'There isn't little milk' contains a double negative that changes the meaning to 'much milk'.
fix: У пакеті багато молока.

en: Whose plan do you prefer? - I prefer Katy and Jill's plan.
current: Чий план ти віддаєш перевагу? - Я віддаю перевагу плану Кеті та Джилл.
issue: The verb 'віддавати перевагу' requires the dative case for the object, not the accusative.
fix: Чийому плану ти віддаєш перевагу? - Я віддаю перевагу плану Кеті та Джилл.

en: How much bread do you eat? - I don't eat bread at all.
current: Скільки хліба ти їси? - Я взагалі не їм хліб.
issue: The word 'хліб' should be in the genitive case after 'не їм' when referring to not eating something at all.
fix: Скільки хліба ти їси? - Я взагалі не їм хліба.

en: It doesn't look good.
current: Це виглядає недобре.
issue: The word order makes the sentence sound unnatural. It should be 'Це не виглядає добре'.
fix: Це не виглядає добре.

en: What does Mr Porter prefer? - He prefers classical music.
current: Що віддає перевагу містер Портер? - Він віддає перевагу класичній музиці.
issue: The verb "віддає перевагу" requires the dative case for the person doing the preferring. The current sentence uses the nominative case.
fix: Чому віддає перевагу містер Портер? - Він віддає перевагу класичній музиці.

en: How much sugar does your wife add? - She doesn't add sugar.
current: Скільки цукру додає твоя дружина? - Вона не додає цукор.
issue: The word for 'sugar' should be in the genitive case because it is the direct object of a negated verb.
fix: Скільки цукру додає твоя дружина? - Вона не додає цукру.

en: You don't live in the city, do you? - Yes, I live in the city.
current: Ти не живеш у місті, чи не так? - Ні, живу в місті.
issue: The 'yes' and 'no' in Ukrainian answers to negative questions are inverted compared to English logic. 'Ні' is used to confirm the negative statement from the question.
fix: Ти не живеш у місті, чи не так? - Так, живу в місті.

en: Your brother doesn't work, does he? - Yes, he works.
current: Твій брат не працює, чи не так? - Ні, працює.
issue: The 'yes' and 'no' in Ukrainian answers to negative questions are inverted compared to English logic. 'Ні' is used to confirm the negative statement from the question.
fix: Твій брат не працює, чи не так? - Так, працює.

en: Is Rob your friend? - Yes, he is.
current: Роб твій друг? - Так, він.
issue: The short answer is incomplete; it should include the verb.
fix: Роб твій друг? - Так, він є.

en: Am I dirty? - Yes, you are.
current: Я брудний? - Так, ти.
issue: The short answer is grammatically incorrect and incomplete.
fix: Я брудний? - Так, ти брудний.

en: Am I clean? - No, you aren't.
current: Я чистий? - Ні, не ти.
issue: The short answer is grammatically incorrect and incomplete.
fix: Я чистий? - Ні, ти не чистий.

en: Running children
current: Біжучі діти
issue: The participle 'біжучі' is not standard and is often considered a Russicism. 'Ті, що біжать' or 'які біжать' is more natural.
fix: Діти, що біжать

en: Working people
current: Працюючі люди
issue: The participle 'працюючі' is not standard and is often considered a Russicism. 'Ті, що працюють' or 'які працюють' is more natural.
fix: Люди, що працюють

en: Sitting boys
current: Сидячі хлопці
issue: The participle 'сидячі' is not standard and is often considered a Russicism. 'Ті, що сидять' or 'які сидять' is more natural.
fix: Хлопці, що сидять

en: Standing girls
current: Стоячі дівчата
issue: The participle 'стоячі' is not standard and is often considered a Russicism. 'Ті, що стоять' or 'які стоять' is more natural.
fix: Дівчата, що стоять

en: Am I speaking too slowly? - No, you aren't.
current: Я говорю надто повільно? - Ні, не ти.
issue: The short answer is grammatically incorrect and unnatural.
fix: Я говорю надто повільно? - Ні, не говориш.

en: She isn't driving a car now, is she? - Yes, she is driving now.
current: Вона зараз не веде машину, чи не так? - Ні, вона зараз веде.
issue: The English answer is affirmative, but the Ukrainian answer is negative.
fix: Вона зараз не веде машину, чи не так? - Так, вона зараз веде.

en: You won't get the present, will you? - Yes, I will get it.
current: Ти не отримаєш подарунок, чи не так? - Ні, отримаю.
issue: The answer should be positive, indicating 'Yes, I will get it'.
fix: Ти не отримаєш подарунок, чи не так? - Так, отримаю.

en: You won't buy all this, will you? - Yes, I will buy.
current: Ти не купиш усе це, чи не так? - Ні, куплю.
issue: The answer should be positive, indicating 'Yes, I will buy'.
fix: Ти не купиш усе це, чи не так? - Так, куплю.

en: Whose neighbour must we call? - Our neighbour.
current: Чийому сусіду ми повинні подзвонити? - Нашому сусіду.
issue: The case of the pronoun "чий" (whose) should be Accusative to match the verb "call" (дзвонити). Also, the short answer "Нашому сусіду" (to our neighbor) is in Dative case, while it should be in Accusative case to match the question "Whose neighbor".
fix: Чийого сусіда ми повинні покликати? - Нашого сусіда.

en: How many speakers must visit the conference? - 10.
current: Скільки спікерів повинні відвідати конференцію? - 10.
issue: The verb 'повинні' should be in the singular neuter form to agree with 'скільки' when referring to inanimate objects, or in the singular masculine if 'спікерів' refers to male speakers only. However, since 'спікерів' is plural, and 'скільки' takes the genitive plural, the verb should be in the neuter singular form 'повинно' for agreement with 'скільки'.
fix: Скільки спікерів повинно відвідати конференцію? - 10.

en: When it doesn't rain, I won't take a taxi.
current: Коли не йде дощ, я не беру таксі.
issue: The English sentence uses future tense, but the Ukrainian translation uses present tense.
fix: Коли не йтиме дощ, я не братиму таксі.

en: We went to our neighbours' house yesterday.
current: Ми вчора ходили до будинку наших сусідів.
issue: The translation uses a prepositional phrase that sounds unnatural in this context.
fix: Ми вчора ходили до сусідів.

en: I dreamt about you last night.
current: Я мріяв про тебе минулої ночі.
issue: The verb 'мріяти' means 'to dream' in the sense of 'to have aspirations' or 'to fantasize', not 'to have a dream while sleeping'.
fix: Я бачив тебе уві сні минулої ночі.

en: We took only a few clothes.
current: Ми взяли лише трохи одягу.
issue: The word 'трохи' is used for uncountable nouns or small quantities, but 'clothes' (одяг) is often treated as a collective noun. For 'a few clothes', which implies distinct items, a more specific phrasing is needed.
fix: Ми взяли лише кілька речей.

en: What was interesting? - Everything was.
current: Що було цікавим? - Усе було.
issue: The instrumental case for 'цікавим' is unnecessary and sounds less natural here.
fix: Що було цікаве? - Усе було.

en: What was useful for you? - His advice.
current: Що було корисним для тебе? - Його порада.
issue: The instrumental case for 'корисним' is unnecessary and sounds less natural here.
fix: Що було корисне для тебе? - Його порада.

en: The flat is rented by a young couple.
current: Квартира орендується молодою парою.
issue: The verb 'орендується' is grammatically correct but using the reflexive passive here sounds less natural. A more common and natural way to express this would be using the active voice with an indefinite subject or a different passive construction.
fix: Квартиру орендує молода пара.

en: The lost dog was found by the police yesterday.
current: Загублена собака була знайдена поліцією вчора.
issue: The word order in the Ukrainian translation is unnatural.
fix: Загубленого собаку було знайдено поліцією вчора.

en: Will the grass be cut the day after tomorrow? - No, it won't.
current: Траву скосить післязавтра? - Ні, не скосить.
issue: The verb 'скосить' is singular, but 'траву' is the object of an impersonal verb, not the subject. The plural form should be used.
fix: Траву скосять післязавтра? - Ні, не скосять.

en: Why were all cookies eaten? - We were hungry.
current: Чому всі печива з’їли? - Ми були голодні.
issue: The word 'печива' is plural, but the English sentence 'all cookies' implies 'all the cookies'. Additionally, 'печиво' is a collective noun, so it should be singular.
fix: Чому все печиво з'їли? - Ми були голодні.

en: What is meant by all this? - I don't know.
current: Що мається на увазі під цим? - Не знаю.
issue: The demonstrative pronoun 'цим' in 'під цим' does not fully convey 'all this'. 'Під усім цим' would be more accurate.
fix: Що мається на увазі під усім цим? - Не знаю.

en: What will be done next? - A new step.
current: Що буде зроблено далі? - Новий крок.
issue: The answer 'Новий крок' (A new step) is grammatically incorrect in response to 'Що буде зроблено далі?' (What will be done next?). It should be a verb phrase, like 'Зробиться новий крок' or 'Новий крок буде зроблено'.
fix: Що буде зроблено далі? - Буде зроблено новий крок.

en: I imagine going far from here.
current: Я уявляю, як далеко піти звідси.
issue: The Ukrainian translation implies 'how to go far' rather than 'going far' as an imagined action.
fix: Я уявляю, як я йду далеко звідси.

en: He always practices speaking English.
current: Він завжди практикує англійську мову.
issue: The Ukrainian translation is missing 'speaking' and only translates 'practices English'.
fix: Він завжди практикує розмовляти англійською мовою.

en: Don't give up making your dreams come true.
current: Не здавайся і втілюй свої мрії.
issue: The conjunction 'і' incorrectly links two separate actions instead of indicating the continuation of the first action.
fix: Не здавайся втілювати свої мрії.

en: The police officer has just found something in his bag.
current: Поліцейський щойно знайшов щось у його сумці.
issue: The possessive pronoun 'його' (his) is redundant and unnatural when referring to the police officer's own bag, as it's implied by context. A native speaker would omit it.
fix: Поліцейський щойно знайшов щось у сумці.

en: Let's meet somewhere close to the city center.
current: Давай зустрінемося десь близько до центру міста.
issue: The word 'близько' means 'near' or 'approximately' when followed by a noun in the genitive case, or it can be an adverb meaning 'closely'. To say 'close to', the preposition 'біля' (near) or 'поруч з' (next to) is more appropriate, or 'недалеко від' (not far from). 'Близько до центру' is not wrong, but 'недалеко від центру' or 'поруч з центром' is more common and natural for 'close to the city center'. Let's use 'недалеко від'.
fix: Давай зустрінемося десь недалеко від центру міста.

en: If I had known about the meeting, I would have attended.
current: Якби я знав(-ла) про зустріч, я б прийшов(прийшла).
issue: The male and female verb forms should be consistent. The English subject 'I' is neutral, so one form should be chosen for the Ukrainian translation.
fix: Якби я знав про зустріч, я б прийшов.

en: Who is that? - That's a woman.
current: ¿Quién es ese? - Es una mujer.
issue: The demonstrative pronoun 'ese' should match the gender of the person being referred to, 'una mujer' is feminine.
fix: ¿Quién es esa? - Es una mujer.

en: Who is that? - That's Ann.
current: ¿Quién es ese? - Es Ann.
issue: The demonstrative pronoun 'ese' should match the gender of the person being referred to, 'Ann' is feminine.
fix: ¿Quién es esa? - Es Ann.

en: Who is that? - That's Katie.
current: ¿Quién es ese? - Es Katie.
issue: The demonstrative pronoun 'ese' should match the gender of the person being referred to, 'Katie' is feminine.
fix: ¿Quién es esa? - Es Katie.

en: Do they do their morning exercises? - No, they don't.
current: ¿Hacen sus ejercicios matutinos? - No, no hacen.
issue: The double negative is missing in the negative answer.
fix: No, no hacen.

en: It looks good.
current: Parece bien.
issue: The verb 'parecer' does not combine with the adverb 'bien' to mean 'it looks good'. Instead, 'parecer' combines with an adjective, such as 'bueno' or 'bonito'. Alternatively, if it refers to something working well, 'funciona bien' would be used.
fix: Se ve bien. / Parece bueno. / Está bien.

en: He doesn't take presents.
current: Él no toma regalos.
issue: The verb 'tomar' implies 'to take' something that is offered, not 'to accept' or 'to receive' presents. A native speaker would likely use 'aceptar' or 'recibir'.
fix: Él no acepta regalos.

en: It doesn't look good.
current: No parece bien.
issue: The phrase 'no parece bien' is not idiomatic for 'it doesn't look good' in the sense of appearance. 'No se ve bien' or 'no tiene buen aspecto' would be more natural.
fix: No se ve bien.

en: Does it look OK? - Yes, it does.
current: ¿Parece bien? - Sí, parece.
issue: The Spanish phrase "Parece bien" is an incorrect translation of "Does it look OK?". The correct translation would be "¿Está bien?" or "¿Se ve bien?". "Parece bien" means "It seems good".
fix: ¿Está bien? - Sí, está.

en: What colour clothes does he wear? - He wears black clothes.
current: ¿Qué color de ropa lleva él? - Lleva ropa negra.
issue: The Spanish phrase for 'What colour' is 'De qué color'.
fix: ¿De qué color de ropa lleva él? - Lleva ropa negra.

en: What colour bag does she want? - She wants a yellow bag.
current: ¿Qué color de bolsa quiere ella? - Quiere una bolsa amarilla.
issue: The Spanish phrase for 'What colour' is 'De qué color'.
fix: ¿De qué color de bolsa quiere ella? - Quiere una bolsa amarilla.

en: Who likes adventures? - I do.
current: ¿Quién ama las aventuras? - Yo.
issue: The verb 'amar' means to love, but 'gustar' is more appropriate for 'to like' in this context.
fix: ¿A quién le gustan las aventuras? - A mí.

en: Who carries your bags? - My friend.
current: ¿Quién lleva tus bolsas? - Mi amigo.
issue: The English word 'bags' can be translated as 'maletas' or 'bolsos' when referring to luggage or handbags, respectively. 'Bolsas' usually refers to plastic bags or grocery bags.
fix: ¿Quién lleva tus maletas? - Mi amigo.

en: Whose son likes adventures? - My son.
current: ¿De quién es hijo al que le gustan las aventuras? - Mi hijo.
issue: The phrase "De quién es hijo al que le gustan las aventuras?" is grammatically incorrect and unnatural.
fix: ¿De quién es el hijo al que le gustan las aventuras? - Mi hijo.

en: Whose sister wants tea? - Their sister.
current: ¿De quién es la hermana que quiere té? - Su hermana.
issue: The translation "Su hermana" for "Their sister" is ambiguous.
fix: De quién es la hermana que quiere té? - La hermana de ellos.

en: They don't like much sugar, do they? - No, they don't like.
current: Ellos no les gusta mucho azúcar, ¿verdad? - No, no les gusta.
issue: The subject pronoun 'Ellos' is redundant when 'les' is already present.
fix: No les gusta mucho azúcar, ¿verdad? - No, no les gusta.

en: Are you carrying all the bags right now? - No, I am not.
current: ¿Estás llevando todas las bolsas ahora? - No, no estoy.
issue: The short answer is grammatically incorrect. The verb 'estar' is missing from the short answer.
fix: ¿Estás llevando todas las bolsas ahora? - No, no lo estoy.

en: She isn't driving a car now, is she? - Yes, she is driving now.
current: Ella no está conduciendo un coche ahora, ¿verdad? - No, ella está conduciendo ahora.
issue: The answer is contradictory, stating 'No' then 'ella está conduciendo ahora' (yes, she is driving now), which is the opposite of the English prompt's expected 'Yes, she is driving now'.
fix: Ella no está conduciendo un coche ahora, ¿verdad? - Sí, ella está conduciendo ahora.

en: Whose children must clean it? - My children.
current: ¿De quién deben limpiar los niños? - Mis niños.
issue: The Spanish translation is missing 'it' and implies 'Whose children must clean?'. The original means 'Whose children must clean it?'.
fix: ¿De quién deben limpiar los niños?

en: Whose assistant must answer the question? - Your assistant.
current: ¿De quién debe responder el asistente? - Tu asistente.
issue: The Spanish translation is missing 'the question' and implies 'Whose assistant must answer?'. The original means 'Whose assistant must answer the question?'.
fix: ¿De quién debe responder el asistente?

en: Whose chair may I take? - You may take my chair.
current: ¿De qué silla puedo tomar? - Puedes tomar mi silla.
issue: The phrase 'De qué silla puedo tomar' is unnatural and literally means 'From what chair can I take'. The correct way to ask 'Whose chair may I take?' should use 'Qué silla puedo tomar' (Which chair can I take?) or 'De quién es la silla que puedo tomar?' (Whose chair can I take?) or similar constructions with 'whose'. 'De qué silla' is typically used when you are asking 'from what chair' something is being done, not 'whose'. The second part of the sentence 'Puedes tomar mi silla' is correct, as 'tomar' here means 'to take' or 'to use'.
fix: ¿Qué silla puedo tomar? - Puedes tomar mi silla.

en: When it doesn't rain, I won't take a taxi.
current: Cuando no llueve, no tomaré un taxi.
issue: The verb 'llover' should be in the subjunctive mood.
fix: Cuando no llueva, no tomaré un taxi.

en: They wanted much money last year.
current: Ellos quisieron mucho dinero el año pasado.
issue: The verb 'querer' in the preterite often implies 'tried' or 'refused', which changes the meaning of the English sentence. For 'wanted', the imperfect tense is more appropriate.
fix: Ellos querían mucho dinero el año pasado.

en: We took only a few clothes.
current: Tomamos solo un poco de ropa.
issue: The English phrase "a few clothes" implies multiple items of clothing, while "un poco de ropa" means "a little bit of clothes" (singular, referring to a quantity).
fix: Tomamos solo unas pocas prendas de ropa.

en: The thief stole all cash.
current: El ladrón robó todo el dinero.
issue: The article 'all' is missing in the Spanish translation.
fix: El ladrón robó todo el dinero en efectivo.

en: Did you see it last time? - Yes, I saw it.
current: ¿Viste esto la última vez? - Sí, lo vi.
issue: The demonstrative pronoun 'esto' changes the meaning of 'it' to 'this'.
fix: ¿Lo viste la última vez? - Sí, lo vi.

en: Did we leave everything here? - No, you didn't leave.
current: ¿Dejamos todo aquí? - No, no dejasteis.
issue: The pronoun 'you' in 'you didn't leave' refers to 'we' in the question, so it should be 'nosotros' or implied, not 'vosotros'. Also, the verb 'dejar' needs an object or a different phrasing.
fix: ¿Dejamos todo aquí? - No, no dejamos.

en: Were we right? - No, you weren't.
current: ¿Teníamos razón? - No, no teníais.
issue: The verb in the negative short answer is incomplete; it should be 'no teníais razón' or 'no la teníais' (referring to 'razón'). The current response is grammatically incomplete and unnatural.
fix: ¿Teníamos razón? - No, no la teníais.

en: The conference will be attended by many doctors.
current: La conferencia será atendida por muchos médicos.
issue: The verb 'atender' is not the most natural choice here; 'asistir' is more appropriate for attending a conference.
fix: La conferencia contará con la asistencia de muchos médicos.

en: The theatre won't be opened next month.
current: El teatro no será abierto el próximo mes.
issue: The past participle of 'abrir' is 'abierto', which is irregular. The verb 'ser' is used correctly in the passive voice.
fix: El teatro no se abrirá el próximo mes.

en: The sofa must be carried upstairs.
current: El sofá debe ser subido arriba.
issue: The word "arriba" is redundant here.
fix: El sofá debe ser subido.

en: Who has just met you at the airport? - Her brother.
current: ¿Quién te ha encontrado en el aeropuerto? - Su hermano.
issue: The Spanish translation is missing the concept of 'just' (recently) meeting someone.
fix: ¿Quién te acaba de encontrar en el aeropuerto? - Su hermano.

en: Who has already sold my watches? - Your son.
current: ¿Quién ya ha vendido mi reloj? - Tu hijo.
issue: The English 'watches' (plural) was translated as 'reloj' (singular).
fix: ¿Quién ya ha vendido mis relojes? - Tu hijo.

en: Whose managers have become popular by now? - Our managers.
current: ¿Los managers de quién se han vuelto populares? - Nuestros managers.
issue: The English 'by now' is missing from the Spanish translation.
fix: ¿Los managers de quién se han vuelto populares a estas alturas? - Nuestros managers.

en: You have visited this place before, haven't you? - Yes, I have.
current: Has visitado este lugar antes, ¿no? - Sí, lo he hecho.
issue: The phrase "lo he hecho" is not the most natural way to say "Yes, I have" in this context. It's too literal.
fix: Has visitado este lugar antes, ¿no? - Sí.

en: Don't give up making your dreams come true.
current: No te rindas en hacer realidad tus sueños.
issue: The preposition 'en' is incorrect after 'rendirse' when followed by an infinitive. It should be 'de' or simply the infinitive.
fix: No te rindas de hacer realidad tus sueños.

en: That's a hat. The hat is black.
current: 모자는 검은색이에요.
issue: The first part of the English sentence, 'That's a hat,' is missing from the Korean translation.
fix: 저것은 모자예요. 모자는 검은색이에요.

en: This is a cat. Is the cat happy? - Yes, it is.
